1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Deep-sky masters -> spatial scene HEICs, via gnomonic compositing onto the star plate.
3	
4	The spatial app is equirect-only (every scene is a 2:1 stereo sphere), but the deep-sky
5	masters in _raw/deepsky/ are FLAT framed astrophotos (a galaxy fills a small slice of real
6	sky, not 360). Feeding one straight to the equirect pipeline would squash a square Carina to
7	2:1. So this adds a COMPOSE stage ahead of the existing depth->stereo->pack:
8	
9	  1. compose  — project the flat master onto a tangent plane at a chosen sky position
10	                (center_lon/lat) and horizontal FOV, gnomonic (rectilinear) so straight
11	                structure doesn't bow, edge-feather it, and ADD it (in linear light) over
12	                the dimmed Deep Star Map equirect. Additive is physically right for emission
13	                on black: dark sky adds nothing so the real stars show through untouched, and
14	                there's no alpha matte to clip the faint galaxy halo. -> mono 2:1 equirect PNG.
15	  2. stereo    — the EXISTING deepspace recipe (synth_pack): near-uniform vergence
16	                (depth_floor 0.94, smooth 0.07, baseline 0.22%, cos^2 poles). Proven on device
17	                to fuse; keeps a whisper of relief. No V100/comfy dependency (luminance depth).
18	  3. pack      — pack_spatial.swift -> Backdrop/spatial_<name>.heic + Thumbnails/<name>.jpg.
19	
20	Placement params below are first guesses (center-ahead, on the equator); expect to nudge
21	FOV / lon / feather / exposure on device. A depth-enhanced variant (DA V2 relief on the
22	pillars) is a possible follow-up A/B but needs the comfy/V100 path — deliberately NOT the
23	default here.
24	
25	2026-07-24, third wrap round: the projection compose above is now the LEGACY path
26	(--legacy). Default is compose_sky360 — every scene becomes a FULL 360 sphere via
27	diffusion outpaint on the pod (sky360.py: outpaint -> seam close -> USDU refine),
28	then RealESRGAN x4 to target, pole soften, and the original high-res master
29	re-composited over its footprint. Rick: immersion and realistic feel supersede
30	accuracy; diffusion first for proportions, upscale second.
31	
32	Run:  python3 upscale/deepsky_pipeline.py                 # all, resumable
33	      python3 upscale/deepsky_pipeline.py --only spatial_m16_pillars --force
34	      python3 upscale/deepsky_pipeline.py --preview spatial_m16_pillars  # mono only, no stereo

117	def _srgb_to_linear(u8):
118	    s = u8.astype(np.float32) / 255.0
119	    return np.where(s <= 0.04045, s / 12.92, ((s + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)

122	def load_base_linear(w, h):
123	    """Deep Star Map plate as linear RGB at (w,h), dimmed. EXR routed through sips (the
124	    Radiance RGBE parser can't read OpenEXR — same reason process_backdrops uses sips)."""
125	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".png", delete=False) as tf:
126	        tmp = tf.name
127	    try:
128	        import subprocess
129	        subprocess.run(["sips", "-s", "format", "png", STARMAP, "--out", tmp],
130	                       check=True, capture_output=True)
131	        im = Image.open(tmp).convert("RGB").resize((w, h), Image.LANCZOS)
132	    finally:
133	        os.unlink(tmp)
134	    return _srgb_to_linear(np.asarray(im, np.uint8)) * BASE_DIM
135	
136	
137	def load_master_linear(rel, rot=0):
138	    """Master as linear RGB, long side capped at MASTER_CAP. `rot` = CCW quarter-turns —
139	    these masters are all ~square or landscape, so rotation reorients vertically-composed
140	    CONTENT (e.g. a towering pillar becomes a horizontal nebula bank); it doesn't change
141	    the wrapped footprint of a square frame."""
142	    im = open_rgb(os.path.join(DEEPSKY, rel))
143	    sw, sh = im.size
144	    scale = MASTER_CAP / max(sw, sh)
145	    if scale < 1.0:
146	        im = im.resize((max(1, round(sw * scale)), max(1, round(sh * scale))), Image.LANCZOS)
147	    arr = _srgb_to_linear(np.asarray(im.convert("RGB"), np.uint8))
148	    if rot:
149	        arr = np.rot90(arr, k=rot).copy()
150	    return arr

153	def _smoothstep(t):
154	    t = np.clip(t, 0.0, 1.0)
155	    return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
156

158	def _bilinear(src, u, v):
159	    """Bilinear sample src[H,W,3] at float coords (u=x, v=y); out-of-range -> 0."""
160	    H, W = src.shape[:2]
161	    x0 = np.floor(u).astype(np.int64); y0 = np.floor(v).astype(np.int64)
162	    x1 = x0 + 1; y1 = y0 + 1
163	    fx = (u - x0)[..., None]; fy = (v - y0)[..., None]
164	    def g(xx, yy):
165	        ok = (xx >= 0) & (xx < W) & (yy >= 0) & (yy < H)
166	        xc = np.clip(xx, 0, W - 1); yc = np.clip(yy, 0, H - 1)
167	        return src[yc, xc] * ok[..., None]
168	    top = g(x0, y0) * (1 - fx) + g(x1, y0) * fx
169	    bot = g(x0, y1) * (1 - fx) + g(x1, y1) * fx
170	    return top * (1 - fy) + bot * fy

173	def _add_layer(base, master, lon0_deg, lat0_deg, fov_x_deg, feather, gain=1.0, lum_key=False,
174	               proj="gnomonic"):
175	    """Project `master` onto the equirect `base` (linear light, additive).
176	
177	    proj="gnomonic": tangent plane — straight structure stays straight, but off-axis it IS
178	    a flat plane ("extends out flat" on device) and edge scale blows up 1/cos^2 (15x at a
179	    150-deg field's edge — the "pixelated" report). Kept for narrow objects (approved look).
180	    proj="equidistant": azimuthal equidistant — uniform angular scale wraps the image around
181	    the viewer, so wide fields curve like a surrounding cloud bank and keep pixel density to
182	    the edge. Nebulae have no straight lines, so the bowing gnomonic avoids is invisible.
183	    """
184	    h, w = base.shape[:2]
185	    sh, sw = master.shape[:2]
186	
187	    lon0 = np.radians(lon0_deg); lat0 = np.radians(lat0_deg)
188	    halfx_ang = np.radians(fov_x_deg) / 2.0          # angular half-width, both projections
189	    if proj == "gnomonic":
190	        xmax = np.tan(halfx_ang)                     # tangent-plane half-width
191	    else:
192	        xmax = halfx_ang                             # plane coords ARE angles
193	    ymax = xmax * (sh / sw)                          # square pixels -> half-height by aspect
194	
195	    # Restrict work to the equirect window the object can touch (+ margin for feather/curve).
196	    half_lon = halfx_ang * 1.15 + np.radians(4)
197	    half_lat = halfx_ang * (sh / sw) * 1.15 + np.radians(4)
198	    c_col = int((lon0 / (2 * np.pi) + 0.5) * w)
199	    c_row = int((0.5 - lat0 / np.pi) * h)
200	    dcol = min(int(np.ceil(half_lon / (2 * np.pi) * w)), w // 2)
201	    drow = int(np.ceil(half_lat / np.pi * h))
202	    r0, r1 = max(0, c_row - drow), min(h, c_row + drow)
203	    cols = np.mod(np.arange(c_col - dcol, c_col + dcol), w)     # wrap-safe column indices
204	
205	    lon = (cols / w - 0.5) * 2 * np.pi                          # [-pi, pi)
206	    lat = (0.5 - np.arange(r0, r1) / h) * np.pi                 # +pi/2 .. -pi/2
207	    LON, LAT = np.meshgrid(lon, lat)
208	    dlon = LON - lon0
209	
210	    cosc = np.sin(lat0) * np.sin(LAT) + np.cos(lat0) * np.cos(LAT) * np.cos(dlon)
211	    if proj == "gnomonic":
212	        front = cosc > 1e-6
213	        denom = np.where(front, cosc, 1.0)
214	    else:
215	        # k = c/sin(c) rescales the sine-based direction components to arc length.
216	        c = np.arccos(np.clip(cosc, -1.0, 1.0))
217	        front = c < np.radians(160)                  # keep well clear of the antipode pole
218	        sinc = np.sin(c)
219	        denom = np.where(sinc > 1e-6, sinc / np.where(c > 1e-6, c, 1.0), 1.0)
220	    Xt = np.cos(LAT) * np.sin(dlon) / denom
221	    Yt = (np.cos(lat0) * np.sin(LAT) - np.sin(lat0) * np.cos(LAT) * np.cos(dlon)) / denom
222	
223	    inside = front & (np.abs(Xt) <= xmax) & (np.abs(Yt) <= ymax)
224	    u = (Xt / xmax * 0.5 + 0.5) * (sw - 1)
225	    v = (0.5 - Yt / ymax * 0.5) * (sh - 1)                      # +Yt = up = row 0
226	    samp = _bilinear(master, u, v)
227	
228	    fx = _smoothstep((xmax - np.abs(Xt)) / (feather * xmax + 1e-9))
229	    fy = _smoothstep((ymax - np.abs(Yt)) / (feather * ymax + 1e-9))
230	    alpha = np.where(inside, np.minimum(fx, fy), 0.0)
231	
232	    if lum_key:
233	        # Discrete objects sit on (near-)black, but the master's background isn't pure zero,
234	        # so the feathered frame reads as a faint rectangular panel. Key on the sampled
235	        # luminance so only the object's own emission contributes and the frame dissolves into
236	        # the real stars. Gentle knee preserves the faint galaxy halo. NOT applied to fields —
237	        # there a luminance key would punch holes in the dark dust lanes that ARE the structure.
238	        Lm = 0.2126 * samp[..., 0] + 0.7152 * samp[..., 1] + 0.0722 * samp[..., 2]
239	        alpha = alpha * _smoothstep((Lm - 0.003) / (0.030 - 0.003))
240	
241	    base[r0:r1, cols] += samp * alpha[..., None] * gain
242

244	def _linear_to_srgb_u8(lin):
245	    s = np.where(lin <= 0.0031308, lin * 12.92, 1.055 * np.clip(lin, 0, 1) ** (1 / 2.4) - 0.055)
246	    return (np.clip(s, 0, 1) * 255 + 0.5).astype(np.uint8)
247

249	def _blur_master(master, long_side=96, up=512):
250	    """Structureless glow copy of the master: crush to ~96px, gaussian, back up to ~512.
251	    In/out are linear light; the PIL round-trip is done in sRGB encoding."""
252	    from PIL import ImageFilter
253	    im = Image.fromarray(_linear_to_srgb_u8(master), "RGB")
254	    sw, sh = im.size
255	    scale = long_side / max(sw, sh)
256	    small = im.resize((max(1, round(sw * scale)), max(1, round(sh * scale))), Image.LANCZOS)
257	    small = small.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(radius=6))
258	    scale = up / max(small.size)
259	    big = small.resize((round(small.size[0] * scale), round(small.size[1] * scale)),
260	                       Image.BILINEAR)
261	    return _srgb_to_linear(np.asarray(big, np.uint8))

264	def compose(rel, kind, p, out_png, w=TARGET_W, h=TARGET_H):
265	    """Star plate + wide blurred glow underlayer + sharp gnomonic master, in linear light.
266	
267	    The halo underlayer (device round-1 fix) spreads the master's own colors well past the
268	    sharp frame at low gain, so the image dissolves into ambient glow instead of ending at a
269	    feathered rectangle floating in darkness.
270	    """
271	    base = load_base_linear(w, h)
272	    master = load_master_linear(rel, rot=p.get("rot", 0))
273	
274	    proj = p.get("proj") or ("equidistant" if kind == "field" else "gnomonic")
275	    # HALO_FOV_MAX guards gnomonic blow-up only; equidistant wraps safely much wider,
276	    # and pano fields (fov >= ~150) need the halo to spread PAST the sharp layer.
277	    halo_fov = min(p["fov_x"] * HALO_FOV_SCALE,
278	                   HALO_FOV_MAX if proj == "gnomonic" else 300.0)
279	    _add_layer(base, _blur_master(master), p["lon"], p["lat"], halo_fov,
280	               feather=0.55, gain=HALO_GAIN[kind], proj=proj)
281	    _add_layer(base, master, p["lon"], p["lat"], p["fov_x"], p["feather"],
282	               lum_key=(kind == "object"), proj=proj)
283	
284	    mono = tonemap(base, exposure=p["exposure"])
285	    Image.fromarray(mono, "RGB").save(out_png)
286	    return (w, h)
287	
288	
289	SKY_CACHE = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/_raw/_sky_cache")
290	
291	# Samples across the footprint for the _paste_master frequency split. Only has to be
292	# fine enough to follow a TONE STEP between the master and the surround (a whole-rect
293	# gradient); anything finer starts transplanting the sky's blurred structure over the
294	# master's real detail. 12 is ~1/12 of the footprint in each axis.
295	LOWPASS_SAMPLES = 12
296	
297	
298	def _wrap_hsmear(strip, nw):
299	    """Horizontally band-limit a row strip to `nw` samples, circularly. Float throughout
300	    (an 8-bit round trip on the smoothest content in the frame, at the zenith, is exactly
301	    where contour rings show) and wrap-padded (a clamped resample leaves a hairline at
302	    lon 180 straight overhead)."""
303	    hh, w = strip.shape[:2]
304	    if nw >= w:
305	        return strip
306	    pad = max(8, w // 64)
307	    padded = np.concatenate([strip[:, -pad:], strip, strip[:, :pad]], axis=1)
308	    pw = max(1, round(nw * (w + 2 * pad) / w))
309	    out = np.empty_like(strip)
310	    for c in range(3):
311	        ch = Image.fromarray(np.ascontiguousarray(padded[..., c], np.float32), "F")
312	        sm = ch.resize((pw, hh), Image.LANCZOS).resize((w + 2 * pad, hh), Image.BILINEAR)
313	        out[..., c] = np.asarray(sm, np.float32)[:, pad:pad + w]
314	    return out
315	
316	
317	def pole_soften(lin, start_deg=60.0, steps=48):
318	    """Kill the zenith/nadir whirlpool by band-limiting azimuthally as 1/cos(lat).
319	
320	    Equirect maps every pixel of the top row onto ONE point. Any azimuthal variation
321	    left up there is therefore wound around that point, which is what reads as a
322	    whirlpool/pinwheel overhead — and diffusion generates the frame with no idea the
323	    projection does this. The previous fix smeared the pole band to a fixed w/16, which
324	    still leaves ~768 distinct values on the top row: a coarser whirlpool, not no
325	    whirlpool.
326	
327	    The projection itself says what the answer is. At latitude `lat` the azimuthal scale
328	    is compressed by cos(lat), so holding ANGULAR resolution constant means low-passing
329	    horizontally to w*cos(lat) samples. That goes to 1 at the pole, i.e. the top row
330	    degenerates to its own mean and there is nothing left to spin. Easing the exponent in
331	    from `start_deg` keeps the useful mid-latitude band at full resolution — applying the
332	    law from the equator would be defensible but would visibly soften the horizon.
333	    """
334	    h, w = lin.shape[:2]
335	    lat = np.abs((0.5 - (np.arange(h) + 0.5) / h) * 180.0)
336	    ramp = _smoothstep((lat - start_deg) / (90.0 - start_deg))
337	    cos = np.clip(np.cos(np.radians(lat)), 1e-9, 1.0)
338	    target = np.clip(w * cos ** ramp, 1.0, w)              # samples this row may carry
339	    # Quantise onto a geometric ladder so each pole costs ~`steps` strip resamples
340	    # rather than one per row.
341	    ladder = np.unique(np.round(np.geomspace(1, w, steps)).astype(np.int64))
342	    idx = np.searchsorted(ladder, target)                  # first ladder >= target
343	    idx = np.clip(idx, 0, len(ladder) - 1)
344	    out = lin.copy()
345	    for j in np.unique(idx):
346	        nw = int(ladder[j])
347	        if nw >= w:
348	            continue
349	        rows = np.flatnonzero(idx == j)
350	        # `lat` is symmetric about the equator, so each level matches a run near the TOP
351	        # and another near the BOTTOM. Taking rows[0]..rows[-1] as one span would smear
352	        # everything in between, i.e. the whole frame.
353	        for run in np.split(rows, np.flatnonzero(np.diff(rows) != 1) + 1):
354	            out[run[0]:run[-1] + 1] = _wrap_hsmear(lin[run[0]:run[-1] + 1], nw)
355	    return out
356

358	def _paste_master(base, master_lin, fov_x, lat, feather):
359	    """Re-composite the original high-res master (linear) over its footprint on the
360	    SR'd sky, feather-edged lerp — real detail survives the round-trip through the
361	    1536px diffusion canvas; the surround stays hallucinated."""
362	    h, w = base.shape[:2]
363	    sh, sw = master_lin.shape[:2]
364	    wf = int(round(w * fov_x / 360.0))
365	    hf = min(int(round(wf * sh / sw)), h)
366	    x0 = (w - wf) // 2
367	    y0 = max(0, min(h - hf, int(round(h * (0.5 - lat / 180.0) - hf / 2))))
368	    if wf > sw * 1.25:
369	        log(f"  WARN: master upscaled x{wf / sw:.2f} into its footprint "
370	            f"(neural-SR candidate — run master_sr.py)")
371	    im = Image.fromarray(_linear_to_srgb_u8(master_lin), "RGB").resize((wf, hf), Image.LANCZOS)
372	    m = _srgb_to_linear(np.asarray(im, np.uint8))
373	
374	    def _lowpass(a):
375	        # cheap large-radius low-pass: downscale to LOWPASS_SAMPLES across the footprint,
376	        # back up. Float ('F') per channel — an 8-bit round-trip would posterize
377	        # linear-space darks.
378	        #
379	        # The sample COUNT is fixed, not the pixel size. It used to downscale to a fixed
380	        # 128 px wide, which is scale-dependent: across a 261deg pano footprint that is a
381	        # ~70 px cutoff (genuinely low-frequency), but across an 85deg object footprint it
382	        # is ~23 px — high enough to carry real structure. So on object scenes the split
383	        # was subtracting the MASTER's galaxies and adding back the SKY's, and the sky's
384	        # copy of them is the 1536 canvas blown up x8: fat blobs with ESRGAN ring halos.
385	        # That is the "galaxy clusters upscale as blobs" report — the pipeline was
386	        # substituting its own blurred rendering for the sharp originals it had just
387	        # pasted, on exactly the scenes with lots of small background objects.
388	        h2, w2 = a.shape[:2]
389	        lo_w = min(LOWPASS_SAMPLES, w2)
390	        lo_h = max(1, round(lo_w * h2 / w2))
391	        out = np.empty((h2, w2, 3), np.float32)
392	        for c in range(3):
393	            ch = Image.fromarray(np.ascontiguousarray(a[..., c], np.float32), "F")
394	            out[..., c] = np.asarray(ch.resize((lo_w, lo_h), Image.LANCZOS)
395	                                     .resize((w2, h2), Image.BILINEAR), np.float32)
396	        return out
397	
398	    # Frequency-split composite (pilot round 2: a soft alpha alone still shows the
399	    # rectangle as a low-frequency tone step — the VAE/USDU round-trip shifts the
400	    # surround's tone relative to the original master). Force the master's low-pass
401	    # field to equal the sky's under its footprint; only real high-frequency detail
402	    # is added, so no tone boundary can survive.
403	    sky_rect = base[y0:y0 + hf, x0:x0 + wf]
404	    m = np.clip(m + _lowpass(sky_rect) - _lowpass(m), 0.0, None)
405	    fx = _smoothstep(np.minimum(np.arange(wf), np.arange(wf)[::-1]) / (feather * wf + 1e-9))
406	    fy = _smoothstep(np.minimum(np.arange(hf), np.arange(hf)[::-1]) / (feather * hf + 1e-9))
407	    a = np.minimum(fx[None, :], fy[:, None])[..., None]
408	    base[y0:y0 + hf, x0:x0 + wf] = sky_rect * (1 - a) + m * a
409

411	def compose_sky360(name, rel, kind, p, out_png, w=TARGET_W, h=TARGET_H):
412	    """Full-360 scene: diffusion sky (sky360.py) -> ESRGAN x4 to target -> pole
413	    soften -> original master re-composited. Mono equirect out, ready for synth_pack."""
414	    from sky360 import make_sky, SKY_RECIPE
415	    from neural_sr import sr_equirect
416	    master_lin = load_master_linear(rel, rot=p.get("rot", 0))
417	    master_u8 = Image.fromarray(_linear_to_srgb_u8(master_lin), "RGB")
418	    desc = p.get("desc") or HAND_DESC.get(name, "a deep space nebula")
419	    from sky360 import FOOT_FEATHER
420	    refined = make_sky(name, master_u8, p["fov_x"], p.get("lat", 0), desc, SKY_CACHE,

422	    sr_png = os.path.join(SKY_CACHE, f"{name}_{SKY_RECIPE}_sr{w}.png")
423	    if os.path.exists(sr_png):
424	        sky = Image.open(sr_png).convert("RGB")
425	        log("  SR: cached")
426	    else:
427	        sky = sr_equirect(Image.open(refined).convert("RGB"), f"{name}_sky", w)
428	        sky.save(sr_png)
429	    base = _srgb_to_linear(np.asarray(sky, np.uint8))
430	    base = pole_soften(base)
431	    # feather comes from sky360, NOT the manifest: the manifest's `feather` is a legacy

433	    _paste_master(base, master_lin, p["fov_x"], p.get("lat", 0), FOOT_FEATHER[kind])

438	def process(name, rel, kind, p, force, preview, legacy=False):
439	    out = os.path.join(BACKDROP, f"{name}.heic")
440	    if os.path.exists(out) and not force and not preview:

455	            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dst), exist_ok=True)
456	            im = Image.open(mono).convert("RGB"); im.thumbnail((2048, 1024), Image.LANCZOS)
457	            im.save(dst, quality=90)

2	"""Neural SR for undersampled POTM masters, on the ai/comfyui V100.
3	
4	Rick's standing rule (2026-07-24): all upscaling is neural inference, never classical
5	resampling. A master is "undersampled" when its pixel density is below the equirect
6	target across its assigned fov: need_px = fov_x/360 * 12288; stretch = need_px / width.
7	Masters with stretch > 1.25 get an UltimateSDUpscale pass (Realistic Vision V6.0 +
8	4x NMKD-Siax — recipe parity with the device-approved Shutterstock upscales) at
9	upscale_by = min(4.0, stretch * 1.15) [node max 4.0], then deepsky_auto.json
10	is repointed at the SR output so the compose stage samples full density.
11	
12	Caveat (verify on device): diffusion SR can hallucinate point sources in star fields.
13	Denoise 0.20 keeps it conservative; A/B the originals if stars look invented.
14	
15	Run:  python3 upscale/master_sr.py            # select + SR + repoint, resumable
16	      python3 upscale/master_sr.py --dry-run  # just list candidates/factors
17	Then: re-compose the affected scenes:
18	      python3 upscale/deepsky_pipeline.py --only <scene> --force   (per scene)
19	"""
20	import argparse
21	import json
22	import os
23	import subprocess
24	import sys
25	import tempfile
26	import time
27	
28	from PIL import Image
29	
30	HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
31	REPO = os.path.dirname(HERE)
32	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "scripts"))
33	from backdrop_tool import open_rgb                                   # noqa: E402
34	
35	Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
36	DEEPSKY = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/_raw/deepsky")
37	SR_DIR = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/_raw/potm_sr")
38	AUTO = os.path.join(HERE, "deepsky_auto.json")
39	TARGET_W = 12288
40	STRETCH_MIN = 1.25
41	NS = "ai"
42	
43	
44	def log(msg):
45	    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True)
46	
47	
48	def comfy_pod():
49	    out = subprocess.run(
50	        ["kubectl", "get", "pods", "-n", NS, "-l", "app=comfyui", "--no-headers",
51	         "-o", "custom-columns=:metadata.name"], capture_output=True, text=True)
52	    return out.stdout.strip().split("\n")[0]
53	
54	
55	def sr_workflow(input_filename, out_prefix, upscale_by):
56	    """API-format UltimateSDUpscale graph (params mirror build_wf.py's approved recipe)."""
57	    return {
58	        "1": {"class_type": "LoadImage", "inputs": {"image": input_filename}},
59	        "2": {"class_type": "CheckpointLoaderSimple",
60	              "inputs": {"ckpt_name": "realisticVisionV60B1_v51VAE.safetensors"}},
61	        "3": {"class_type": "CLIPTextEncode",
62	              "inputs": {"clip": ["2", 1], "text":
63	                         "highly detailed, sharp focus, realistic photograph, natural texture, fine detail"}},
64	        "4": {"class_type": "CLIPTextEncode",
65	              "inputs": {"clip": ["2", 1], "text":
66	                         "blurry, soft, noise, film grain, jpeg artifacts, compression, oversharpened, halo, plastic skin"}},
67	        "5": {"class_type": "UpscaleModelLoader", "inputs": {"model_name": "4x_NMKD-Siax_200k.pth"}},
68	        "6": {"class_type": "UltimateSDUpscale",
69	              "inputs": {"image": ["1", 0], "model": ["2", 0], "positive": ["3", 0],
70	                         "negative": ["4", 0], "vae": ["2", 2], "upscale_model": ["5", 0],
71	                         "upscale_by": upscale_by, "seed": 0, "steps": 18, "cfg": 6.0,
72	                         "sampler_name": "dpmpp_2m", "scheduler": "karras", "denoise": 0.20,
73	                         "mode_type": "Chess", "tile_width": 1024, "tile_height": 1024,
74	                         "mask_blur": 16, "tile_padding": 32, "seam_fix_mode": "Band Pass",
75	                         "seam_fix_denoise": 1.0, "seam_fix_width": 64,
76	                         "seam_fix_mask_blur": 8, "seam_fix_padding": 16,
77	                         "force_uniform_tiles": True, "tiled_decode": True,
78	                         "batch_size": 1}},
79	        "7": {"class_type": "SaveImage",
80	              "inputs": {"filename_prefix": out_prefix, "images": ["6", 0]}},
81	    }
82	
83	
84	def run_pod_sr(pod, src_png, name, upscale_by, out_png):
85	    subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", src_png, f"{NS}/{pod}:/basedir/input/sr_{name}.png"], check=True)
86	    wf = {"prompt": sr_workflow(f"sr_{name}.png", f"srout_{name}", round(upscale_by, 2))}
87	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as tf:
88	        json.dump(wf, tf)
89	        wfp = tf.name
90	    try:
91	        subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", wfp, f"{NS}/{pod}:/tmp/sr_{name}.json"], check=True)
92	    finally:
93	        os.unlink(wfp)
94	    r = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
95	                        f"curl -s -m 15 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8188/prompt "
96	                        f"-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @/tmp/sr_{name}.json"],
97	                       capture_output=True, text=True)
98	    if '"prompt_id"' not in r.stdout:
99	        raise RuntimeError(f"SR submit failed for {name}: {r.stdout[:300]} {r.stderr[:200]}")
100	    for _ in range(900):                                   # up to ~60 min per image
101	                                                           # (a 10k-wide USDU output
102	                                                           # legitimately runs >16 min)
103	        q = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
104	                            "curl -s -m 6 http://127.0.0.1:8188/queue"],
105	                           capture_output=True, text=True)
106	        try:
107	            d = json.loads(q.stdout)
108	            if len(d.get("queue_running", [])) + len(d.get("queue_pending", [])) == 0:
109	                break
110	        except Exception:
111	            pass
112	        time.sleep(4)
113	    ls = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
114	                         f"ls -t /basedir/output/srout_{name}_*.png 2>/dev/null | head -1"],
115	                        capture_output=True, text=True)
116	    remote = ls.stdout.strip()
117	    if not remote:
118	        raise RuntimeError(f"no SR output for {name}")
119	    subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", f"{NS}/{pod}:{remote}", out_png], check=True)
120	
121	
122	def main():
123	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
124	    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
125	    args = ap.parse_args()
126	
127	    rows = json.load(open(AUTO))
128	    cands = []
129	    for r in rows:
130	        if r["rel"].startswith("../potm_sr/"):
131	            continue                                        # already repointed
132	        src = os.path.join(DEEPSKY, r["rel"])
133	        with Image.open(src) as im:
134	            w = im.size[0]
135	        stretch = (r["params"]["fov_x"] / 360 * TARGET_W) / w
136	        if stretch > STRETCH_MIN:
137	            cands.append((r, src, min(4.0, stretch * 1.15)))   # node max is 4.0
138	    log(f"{len(cands)} undersampled master(s)")
139	    for r, src, f in cands:
140	        log(f"  {r['name']}: x{f:.2f}")
141	    if args.dry_run or not cands:
142	        return 0
143	
144	    pod = comfy_pod()
145	    if not pod:
146	        raise SystemExit("no comfyui pod found")
147	    log(f"pod: {pod}")
148	    os.makedirs(SR_DIR, exist_ok=True)
149	    ok = fail = 0
150	    for r, src, factor in cands:
151	        pid = r["name"].removeprefix("spatial_")
152	        out = os.path.join(SR_DIR, f"{pid}.png")
153	        try:
154	            if not os.path.exists(out):
155	                with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
156	                    png = os.path.join(td, f"{pid}.png")
157	                    open_rgb(src).convert("RGB").save(png)
158	                    t0 = time.time()
159	                    run_pod_sr(pod, png, pid, factor, out)
160	                with Image.open(out) as im:
161	                    log(f"  {pid}: SR x{factor:.2f} -> {im.size[0]}x{im.size[1]} ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)")
162	            else:
163	                log(f"  {pid}: SR output exists, skipping pod run")
164	            r["rel"] = f"../potm_sr/{pid}.png"
165	            ok += 1
166	        except Exception as e:                              # noqa: BLE001
167	            fail += 1
168	            log(f"  !! FAILED {pid}: {e}")
169	
170	    with open(AUTO, "w") as f:
171	        json.dump(rows, f, indent=1)
172	    log(f"DONE: {ok} SR'd + repointed, {fail} failed. Re-compose with deepsky_pipeline --force.")
173	    return 1 if fail else 0
174	
175	
176	if __name__ == "__main__":
177	    sys.exit(main())

2	"""Flat deep-sky masters -> full 360 equirect skies, by diffusion outpaint on the V100.
3	
4	Rick's directive (2026-07-24, third round of wrap feedback): partial equidistant wraps
5	(180-270deg) still read as "wider shots", not wraparound. Every deep-sky scene — wide
6	POTM panoramics AND the hand-tuned masters — becomes a FULL 360 sphere. Immersion and
7	realistic feel supersede accuracy to the source photo: the sphere beyond the master is
8	speculative diffusion. Ordering is also his: diffusion first at working res to get the
9	proportions right and convert to equirect, THEN neural upscale to target res.
10	
11	Stages (per scene, each cached in _raw/_sky_cache/):
12	  1. outpaint  — master placed on a 1536x768 2:1 canvas at its natural angular
13	                 proportions (fov_x of 360 wide, height by aspect), rest masked;
14	                 RV6.0 inpaint at denoise 1.0 hallucinates the surrounding sky.
15	  2. seam      — roll 180deg, mirror-blend the (now centered) lon join so it is
16	                 continuous to the pixel, then repaint that band at LOW denoise to break
17	                 the mirror symmetry without letting the prompt re-tint it.
18	  (3. refine   — an UltimateSDUpscale x2 used to sit here. It is off by default and kept
19	                 only for A/B: it tiled the dark sky into a visible grid. See
20	                 REFINE_BACKEND.)
21	Downstream (deepsky_pipeline.compose_sky360): RealESRGAN multi-pass -> 12288x6144, pole
22	soften, then the ORIGINAL high-res master is re-composited over its footprint so real
23	detail survives the round-trip through working res.
24	
25	Seeds are fixed per scene name (crc32) so re-runs reproduce. Both workflows are
26	mirrored in the ComfyUI web UI (build_sr_wf_ui.py): equirect_360_outpaint,
27	equirect_360_usdu_refine.

59	                                    # master's edges; USDU invents the detail
60	SEAM_DENOISE = 0.40                 # round 6 (was 0.70): the seam band is now continuous
61	                                    # BY CONSTRUCTION (mirror blend, see _mirror_blend_seam)
62	                                    # so diffusion only has to break the mirror symmetry.
63	                                    # At 0.70 the prompt re-tinted the band — on device the
64	                                    # Phantom Galaxy's warm sky grew a cool purple stripe
65	                                    # down 180deg that read as a vertical bruise. Measured:
66	                                    # the R-B axis swung +29 -> -11 -> +5 across the band
67	                                    # with no pixel-level step, i.e. a palette failure, not
68	                                    # a continuity failure — so lower the denoise, don't
69	                                    # widen the mask
70	FILL_BLUR = 32                      # px, near-rect fill: local continuation structure
71	FILL_BLUR_FAR = 128                 # px, far-field fill: round 4 left ghost COPIES of
72	                                    # the master (mirror tiles at blur 32 kept its
73	                                    # morphology, which denoise 0.65 preserved) — far
74	                                    # from the rect only a structureless wash remains
75	GHOST_DIST = 256                    # px over which near fill fades to far fill
76	FILL_DETAIL = 0.35                  # fraction of the master's FINE texture (detail finer
77	                                    # than FILL_BLUR) added back into the FAR fill. The
78	                                    # anchor dominance that fixed the palette problem is
79	                                    # also what left the far surround a structureless
80	                                    # wash: at denoise 0.65 diffusion faithfully continues
81	                                    # a blur-128 anchor, and a blurred anchor produces
82	                                    # blurred sky. Feeding back the high band only gives
83	                                    # it something to develop into stars/filaments without
84	                                    # touching the LOW band, which is where round 4's ghost
85	                                    # copies of the master lived (morphology coarser than
86	                                    # FILL_BLUR) — different frequency band, so this does
87	                                    # not reopen that failure
88	MASK_BLUR = 24                      # soft mask edge; true master pixels return in the
89	                                    # final-res re-composite anyway
90	MASK_OVERLAP = 48                   # px floor for how far the generation ring reaches
91	                                    # INTO the master; FOOT_FEATHER normally sets it
92	# How far the master dissolves into the surround, as a fraction of its own footprint.
93	# This is ONE number used twice and the two uses must agree: build_canvas fades the
94	# master into the fill over it, and deepsky_pipeline._paste_master fades the true
95	# high-res master back in over it at final res. If they disagreed you would get real
96	# detail returning inside a ring the sky had already blurred, i.e. the hard edge back.
97	# Fields dissolve further (they are meant to read as surrounding cloud, device round 1);
98	# objects less, so the hero does not lose its own outline.
99	FOOT_FEATHER = {"field": 0.22, "object": 0.14}
100	REFINE_DENOISE = 0.30               # higher than SR's 0.20: we WANT invented detail
101	REFINE_BY = 2.0                     # 1536x768 -> 3072x1536 (then ESRGAN x4 = 12288)
102	
103	# Which x2 refine sits between the outpaint and the ESRGAN run up to target.
104	#   "none" (default) — no diffusion refine; neural_sr multi-passes RealESRGAN 1536 -> 12288.
105	#   "usdu"           — the UltimateSDUpscale pass, kept switchable for A/B only.
106	# Round 6, on device: USDU is the source of the "banding on pretty much every image"
107	# report. It tiles a near-flat dark sky and each tile's VAE round-trip lands on its own
108	# black level, so the 12288 sky carries a visible 1024-tile grid of tone steps; the
109	# "Band Pass" seam fix then draws a DARK LINE down every tile join at denoise 1.0.
110	# Confirmed by stage inspection: the 1536 outpaint is clean, the 3072 refine has the grid.
111	# This is also just neural_sr.py's own A/B finding (RealESRGAN beats USDU on equirect
112	# starfields, "no tile seams") re-learned the hard way — the refine stage reintroduced
113	# the loser. The cost of "none" is that the hallucinated surround keeps whatever detail
114	# the outpaint gave it; invent structure THERE, not in a tiled post-pass.
115	REFINE_BACKEND = os.environ.get("SKY360_REFINE", "none")
116	
117	# Bump when a stage's recipe changes. It is part of every cache filename, so a recipe
118	# change can never silently reuse an old render — the previous round's near-miss was an
119	# `[or]*` glob that cleared two of a scene's three stage files and left the third.
120	# Old-tag files are just dead weight in the (gitignored) cache; delete them when happy.
121	SKY_RECIPE = "r7"
122	
123	# The field prompt has to ask for CONTINUATION, not surroundings. These masters are
124	# crops: the subject runs past every frame edge, so "deep space surrounding X" invites
125	# the model to stop X at the frame and start sky — which is exactly the galaxy-ends-in-
126	# a-box report on the Phantom Galaxy. Naming the structure that must keep going gives
127	# the outpaint something to extend.
128	POS_TMPL = ("seamless 360 degree equirectangular panorama, {desc} continuing outward in "
129	            "every direction beyond the frame, spiral arms and dust lanes and nebulosity "
130	            "extending and fading into the distance, vast starfield, tiny distant "
131	            "background galaxies, photorealistic astrophotography, deep black sky")
132	# Objects/planets hang on (near-)black: the mirror-tile fill turns into ghost COPIES
133	# (batch 1: Saturn grew extra planets, Andromeda a twin swirl) and flat dark surrounds
134	# show USDU tile seams. Their fill is a flat estimate of the master's own border sky,
135	# denoise high, prompt = starfield — prompt dominance is CORRECT here.
136	POS_OBJ = ("seamless 360 degree equirectangular deep space starfield surrounding "
137	           "{desc}, vast field of scattered stars, tiny distant stars, tiny faint "
138	           "remote background galaxies, deep black sky, photorealistic astrophotography")
139	OBJ_DENOISE = 0.85
140	NEG = ("text, watermark, signature, caption, border, frame, vignette, planet earth, "
141	       "ground, terrain, horizon, people, spacecraft, window, lens flare, blurry, "
142	       "lowres, jpeg artifacts, oversaturated")
143	NEG_OBJ = NEG + ", planet, planets, moon, moons, glowing orb, sphere, planetary rings"

154	def outpaint_wf(canvas_name, mask_name, prompt, seed, out_prefix,
155	                denoise=OUTPAINT_DENOISE, neg=NEG):
156	    """API-format init-anchored outpaint: masked region regenerates FROM the canvas's
157	    blurred fill (VAEEncode + SetLatentNoiseMask), unmasked master stays."""
158	    return {
159	        "1": {"class_type": "LoadImage", "inputs": {"image": canvas_name}},
160	        "2": {"class_type": "LoadImageMask", "inputs": {"image": mask_name, "channel": "red"}},
161	        "3": {"class_type": "CheckpointLoaderSimple", "inputs": {"ckpt_name": CKPT}},
162	        "4": {"class_type": "CLIPTextEncode", "inputs": {"clip": ["3", 1], "text": prompt}},

169	                         "latent_image": ["10", 0], "seed": seed, "steps": OUTPAINT_STEPS,
170	                         "cfg": OUTPAINT_CFG, "sampler_name": "dpmpp_2m",
171	                         "scheduler": "karras", "denoise": denoise}},
172	        "8": {"class_type": "VAEDecode", "inputs": {"samples": ["7", 0], "vae": ["3", 2]}},

180	    space prompt (we're inventing detail in hallucinated sky, not preserving a photo)."""

194	                         # every tile join on dark sky, so seam fixing is off and the
195	                         # padding/blur are wide enough to soften the per-tile tone steps
196	                         # it cannot remove. See REFINE_BACKEND for why this is not default.
197	                         "denoise": REFINE_DENOISE, "mode_type": "Chess",

214	def _run(pod, wf, tag, out_png, timeout_s=3600):
215	    """Submit an API workflow, poll the queue to idle, fetch the newest output."""
216	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as tf:
217	        json.dump({"prompt": wf}, tf)
218	        wfp = tf.name
219	    try:
220	        subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", wfp, f"{NS}/{pod}:/tmp/sky_{tag}.json"], check=True)
221	    finally:
222	        os.unlink(wfp)
223	    r = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
224	                        f"curl -s -m 15 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8188/prompt "
225	                        f"-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @/tmp/sky_{tag}.json"],
226	                       capture_output=True, text=True)
227	    if '"prompt_id"' not in r.stdout:
228	        raise RuntimeError(f"submit failed for {tag}: {r.stdout[:300]} {r.stderr[:200]}")
229	    t0 = time.time()
230	    while time.time() - t0 < timeout_s:
231	        q = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
232	                            "curl -s -m 6 http://127.0.0.1:8188/queue"],
233	                           capture_output=True, text=True)
234	        try:
235	            d = json.loads(q.stdout)
236	            if len(d.get("queue_running", [])) + len(d.get("queue_pending", [])) == 0:
237	                break
238	        except Exception:
239	            pass
240	        time.sleep(4)
241	    ls = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "exec", "-n", NS, pod, "--", "bash", "-lc",
242	                         f"ls -t /basedir/output/{tag}_*.png 2>/dev/null | head -1"],
243	                        capture_output=True, text=True)
244	    remote = ls.stdout.strip()
245	    if not remote:
246	        raise RuntimeError(f"no output for {tag} (check the pod queue before resubmitting)")
247	    subprocess.run(["kubectl", "cp", f"{NS}/{pod}:{remote}", out_png], check=True)

250	def _mirror_map(coords, period):
251	    """Signed coords mapped onto a mirror-tiled source of size `period`."""
252	    m = np.mod(coords, 2 * period)
253	    return np.where(m < period, m, 2 * period - 1 - m)
254	
255	
256	def _smoothstep(t):
257	    t = np.clip(t, 0.0, 1.0)
258	    return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
259	
260	
261	def _mirror_blend_seam(rolled, band=SEAM_BAND):
262	    """Close the (now centred) lon join BY CONSTRUCTION, before any diffusion touches it.
263	
264	    Over a band centred on the join, cross-fade each side with the mirror of the other
265	    side. Weight is exactly 0.5 at the join, so both bounding columns resolve to the same
266	    average and the join is continuous to the pixel; it decays to 0 at the band edge, so
267	    the original content returns smoothly. The band is left mirror-symmetric, which the
268	    following low-denoise pass breaks up — but the palette on each side is the local one,
269	    which is what a free-prompt band at denoise 0.70 could not guarantee (see SEAM_DENOISE).
270	    """
271	    out = rolled.astype(np.float32).copy()
272	    cx = rolled.shape[1] // 2
273	    h = band // 2
274	    w = 0.5 * (1.0 - _smoothstep(np.arange(1, h + 1, dtype=np.float32) / h))   # 0.5 -> 0
275	    left = out[:, cx - h:cx].copy()
276	    right = out[:, cx:cx + h].copy()
277	    wl = w[::-1][None, :, None]                 # left band: weight grows toward the join
278	    wr = w[None, :, None]                       # right band: weight falls from the join
279	    out[:, cx - h:cx] = left * (1 - wl) + right[:, ::-1] * wl
280	    out[:, cx:cx + h] = right * (1 - wr) + left[:, ::-1] * wr
281	    return np.clip(out + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
282	
283	
284	def build_canvas(master_im, fov_x, lat, kind="field"):
285	    """Place the master on a 2:1 canvas at its natural angular proportions. The rest
286	    of the canvas is a mirror-tiled + heavily blurred extension of the master — the
287	    init image that anchors the outpaint to the master's own palette (see
288	    OUTPAINT_DENOISE note). Returns (canvas u8 HxWx3, mask u8 HxW — 255 = generate,
289	    soft-edged)."""
290	    from PIL import ImageFilter
291	    sw, sh = master_im.size
292	    wf = int(round(WORK_W * fov_x / 360.0))
293	    hf = min(int(round(wf * sh / sw)), WORK_H)
294	    x0 = (WORK_W - wf) // 2
295	    y0 = int(round(WORK_H * (0.5 - lat / 180.0) - hf / 2))
296	    y0 = max(0, min(WORK_H - hf, y0))
297	    small = np.asarray(master_im.resize((wf, hf), Image.LANCZOS), np.uint8)
298	    if kind == "object":
299	        # flat fill at the master's own border-sky level — no structure, no ghosts
300	        ring = np.concatenate([small[:4].reshape(-1, 3), small[-4:].reshape(-1, 3),
301	                               small[:, :4].reshape(-1, 3), small[:, -4:].reshape(-1, 3)])
302	        fill = np.broadcast_to(np.median(ring, axis=0).astype(np.uint8),
303	                               (WORK_H, WORK_W, 3)).copy()
304	    else:
305	        tiled = small[np.ix_(_mirror_map(np.arange(WORK_H) - y0, hf),
306	                             _mirror_map(np.arange(WORK_W) - x0, wf))]
307	        tiled_im = Image.fromarray(tiled, "RGB")
308	        near = np.asarray(tiled_im.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(FILL_BLUR)), np.float32)
309	        far = np.asarray(tiled_im.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(FILL_BLUR_FAR)), np.float32)
310	        dx = np.maximum(np.maximum(x0 - np.arange(WORK_W), np.arange(WORK_W) - (x0 + wf - 1)), 0)
311	        dy = np.maximum(np.maximum(y0 - np.arange(WORK_H), np.arange(WORK_H) - (y0 + hf - 1)), 0)
312	        t = np.clip(np.hypot(dx[None, :], dy[:, None]) / GHOST_DIST, 0.0, 1.0)[..., None]
313	        # Fine texture goes back into the far field only — the near field already carries
314	        # blur-32 structure; it is the far wash that gives diffusion nothing to work with.
315	        detail = (np.asarray(tiled_im, np.float32) - near) * FILL_DETAIL
316	        fill = (near * (1 - t) + (far + detail) * t + 0.5)
317	        fill = np.clip(fill, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
318	    # Feather the master INTO its own fill rather than butting a hard rect against it.
319	    # Round 6, on device: a hard rect leaves an edge that NOTHING downstream can remove —
320	    # the sharp-astrophoto-vs-hallucinated-wash boundary is baked into the sky here, at
321	    # the outpaint, so feathering the final re-composite just fades true detail back in
322	    # ON TOP of an edge that is already there. Blending it in over a wide ramp, and
323	    # letting the generation mask cover that whole ramp, means the density falls off
324	    # gradually and there is no boundary for USDU/ESRGAN to crisp up later.
325	    fr = FOOT_FEATHER[kind]
326	    ax = _smoothstep(np.minimum(np.arange(wf), np.arange(wf)[::-1]) / (fr * wf + 1e-9))
327	    ay = _smoothstep(np.minimum(np.arange(hf), np.arange(hf)[::-1]) / (fr * hf + 1e-9))
328	    a = np.minimum(ax[None, :], ay[:, None])[..., None]
329	    canvas = fill.astype(np.float32)
330	    rect = canvas[y0:y0 + hf, x0:x0 + wf]
331	    canvas[y0:y0 + hf, x0:x0 + wf] = rect * (1 - a) + small.astype(np.float32) * a
332	    canvas = np.clip(canvas + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
333	    # Generate everywhere except the core the master fully owns — i.e. the whole feather
334	    # ring is diffusion's to paint, anchored by the already-smooth blend underneath it.
335	    ovx = max(MASK_OVERLAP, int(fr * wf))
336	    ovy = max(MASK_OVERLAP // 2, int(fr * hf))
337	    mask = np.full((WORK_H, WORK_W), 255, np.uint8)
338	    mask[y0 + ovy:y0 + hf - ovy, x0 + ovx:x0 + wf - ovx] = 0
339	    mask = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(mask, "L").filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(MASK_BLUR)), np.uint8)
340	    return canvas, mask
341	
342	
343	def make_sky(name, master_im, fov_x, lat, desc, cache_dir, kind="field",
344	             refine=REFINE_BACKEND):
345	    """Master (PIL RGB, already rotated) -> full-360 sky PNG path (1536x768 with the
346	    default `refine="none"`, 3072x1536 with `refine="usdu"`). Each pod stage is cached;
347	    delete the cache file(s) to force a stage to re-run."""
348	    os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
349	    stem = f"{name}_{SKY_RECIPE}"
350	    refined = os.path.join(cache_dir, f"{stem}_refined.png")
351	    if refine == "usdu" and os.path.exists(refined):
352	        return refined
353	    prompt = (POS_OBJ if kind == "object" else POS_TMPL).format(desc=desc)
354	    denoise = OBJ_DENOISE if kind == "object" else OUTPAINT_DENOISE
355	    neg = NEG_OBJ if kind == "object" else NEG
356	    seed = scene_seed(name)
357	    pod = comfy_pod()
358	    outp = os.path.join(cache_dir, f"{stem}_outpaint.png")
359	    if not os.path.exists(outp):
360	        canvas, mask = build_canvas(master_im, fov_x, lat, kind)
361	        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
362	            cp, mp = os.path.join(td, "c.png"), os.path.join(td, "m.png")
363	            Image.fromarray(canvas, "RGB").save(cp)
364	            Image.fromarray(mask, "L").save(mp)
365	            _upload(pod, cp, f"sky_{name}_canvas.png")
366	            _upload(pod, mp, f"sky_{name}_mask.png")
367	            t0 = time.time()
368	            o1 = os.path.join(td, "o1.png")
369	            _run(pod, outpaint_wf(f"sky_{name}_canvas.png", f"sky_{name}_mask.png",
370	                                  prompt, seed, f"skyout_{name}", denoise=denoise,
371	                                  neg=neg), f"skyout_{name}", o1)
372	            _log(f"  {name}: outpaint ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
373	            # close the lon seam: roll 180deg, mirror-blend the join continuous, repaint
374	            # the band at low denoise to break the mirror symmetry, roll back
375	            img = np.asarray(Image.open(o1).convert("RGB"), np.uint8)
376	            rolled = _mirror_blend_seam(np.roll(img, WORK_W // 2, axis=1))
377	            from PIL import ImageFilter
378	            band = np.zeros((WORK_H, WORK_W), np.uint8)
379	            cx = WORK_W // 2
380	            band[:, cx - SEAM_BAND // 2: cx + SEAM_BAND // 2] = 255
381	            band = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(band, "L")
382	                              .filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(MASK_BLUR)), np.uint8)
383	            rp, bp = os.path.join(td, "r.png"), os.path.join(td, "b.png")
384	            Image.fromarray(rolled, "RGB").save(rp)
385	            Image.fromarray(band, "L").save(bp)
386	            _upload(pod, rp, f"sky_{name}_rolled.png")
387	            _upload(pod, bp, f"sky_{name}_band.png")
388	            t0 = time.time()
389	            o2 = os.path.join(td, "o2.png")
390	            _run(pod, outpaint_wf(f"sky_{name}_rolled.png", f"sky_{name}_band.png",
391	                                  prompt, seed + 1, f"skyseam_{name}",
392	                                  denoise=SEAM_DENOISE, neg=neg), f"skyseam_{name}", o2)
393	            img = np.asarray(Image.open(o2).convert("RGB"), np.uint8)
394	            Image.fromarray(np.roll(img, -(WORK_W // 2), axis=1), "RGB").save(outp)
395	            _log(f"  {name}: seam close ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
396	    if refine != "usdu":
397	        return outp
398	    _upload(pod, outp, f"sky_{name}_outpaint.png")
399	    t0 = time.time()
400	    _run(pod, refine_wf(f"sky_{name}_outpaint.png", prompt, seed + 2,
401	                        f"skyref_{name}"), f"skyref_{name}", refined)
402	    _log(f"  {name}: USDU refine x{REFINE_BY:.0f} ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
403	    return refined

content.text:
Renamed `screenshots ` → `screenshots`.

Here's what I found. The headline: **every scene you flagged is a pre-fix r6 render.** Only potm2208a, potm2410a and potm2210a on disk are r7 — the 33 others still hold last session's output, so three of your six complaints are things the committed code already targets. But two are *not* fixed, and I verified that against the current code, not the handoff's claims.

## The three screenshots

**potm2307a — "just an image in a box."** Worse than a box edge: the outpaint stage returned nothing. `_sky_cache/spatial_potm2307a_outpaint.png` is a flat grey-brown wash with zero structure and the master pasted on it as a hard rectangle. The whole sphere outside the footprint is that wash plus USDU tile lines. r7 will remove the hard edge (canvas-side feather) but this is the same failure as the potm2208a "milky surround" the handoff left open — the far fill has no distance falloff, so you'd trade a grey box for a grey sphere.

**m8_lagoon — "gaps between the stitches."** Mirror-tile ghosting. You're seeing three copies of the Lagoon — the real master centre, mirrored copies left and right — with black gutters between them where the master's own dark frame edge meets its mirror. **This is not fixed.** I rebuilt the outpaint anchor with today's code (`m8_canvas_r7.png` in scratchpad) and it produces the identical triptych with the identical dark gutters. `GHOST_DIST=256` fades near-fill to far-fill over 256px, but the mirror period here is the 614px footprint, so the copies sit in the "far" zone — and blur-128 softens a 614px-wide morphology, it doesn't destroy it. `FILL_DETAIL=0.35` then adds the sharp texture back on top, so r7 will make these ghosts *crisper* than r6.

**spherex_stars — banding.** I can't reproduce it, and I want to flag that rather than guess. The shipped equirect measures clean everywhere: its smoothest 512px patch carries 176–244 distinct levels per channel with 1–10px flat runs. The screenshot itself measures 13–31px flat runs, ~100 distinct levels — no posterization, no tile grid under high-pass. Also worth knowing: spherex_stars doesn't touch sky360 at all. It's a native 4000×2000 survey equirect through `process_backdrops.py` → RealESRGAN → pack. So the USDU-refine fix does nothing for it, and `pole_soften` never runs on that path. Can you point at where in the frame the bands are? If it's the milky wash across the bottom, that's the nadir region and a different problem.

## Your two questions

**saturn1 upscaling.** ESA's "original" is a web-sized file, ~1103×621 (0.7 MP) — the manifest records it at 2.06 MB. `master_sr.py` measured stretch against the 95° footprint and ran UltimateSDUpscale at ×3.38 to 3720×2096. That's the pixelation: at denoise 0.20 the 4x_NMKD-Siax model quantizes Saturn's soft limb into hard ~10px staircase steps, and the 1024px chess tiles land across the ring ansae — visible as blocky black notches at both ring tips and ringing along the rings. The USDU tile grid is also visible in the surrounding dark sky. Note this is the *same* recipe (Band Pass seam fix, denoise 1.0) that you already condemned as the banding source in sky360; `master_sr.py` still has it.

**m31_andromeda / ngc4631_whale — "images stacked on top of each other."** Three things at once:
1. The outpaint painted a *second* galaxy. m31's outpaint has a twin Andromeda in the upper right and continues the disc at a different tilt than the master's. Cause: `POS_OBJ` names the subject — "starfield surrounding *the vast Andromeda Galaxy*" — at denoise 0.85. `NEG_OBJ` blocks planets and moons (added after Saturn grew extra planets) but says nothing about galaxies. **Also not fixed** — and m31/whale are hand rows with `kind` hardcoded in `MANIFEST`, so the new measured-kind logic in `potm_auto_manifest.py` never touches them.
2. The hard footprint rectangle — visible as a lighter panel with straight edges in the whale composite. That one r7 does fix.
3. The soft blue blobs down the whale's right side — the `LOWPASS_SAMPLES` bug. Also fixed in r7.

Evidence crops are in the scratchpad: `whale_foot.png`, `saturn_foot.png`, `saturn_crop1to1.png`, `potm2307a_full.png`, `m8_lagoon_full.png`, `m8_canvas_r7.png`.

## What I'd want your call on before any re-render

Two defects survive into r7 and would come back on all 36 scenes: the mirror-tile ghosting on wide `field` masters, and prompt-induced duplicate subjects on `object` masters. Both are cheap to test — the anchor build runs locally in seconds, and a single-scene outpaint is ~2 min on the pod. Want me to work up fixes for those two before the full run, or re-render as-is and judge in the headset?

Work up the fixes and let's do the full run. I'm losing track of what's fixed where but not in place yet. I put a couple of lines on the image from spherex_stars. The screenshot makes them almost invisible, but they're very pronounced in the 3D space.

`stereo_synth.py:124` rounds disparity to whole pixels. The deepspace recipe gives each eye a half-disparity of `0.5 × 0.0022 × 12288 × depth × cos²(lat)` = up to 13.5 px, and `cos²(lat)` sweeps that smoothly to zero at the poles — so `round()` carves it into **13 integer terraces per hemisphere at fixed latitudes**, independent of image content. Each terrace boundary is a 1 px content step in each eye and a discrete jump in apparent depth between them. That's why it's pronounced in the headset and nearly invisible in a screenshot. Predicted band spacing at mid-latitude is 25–50 px of view; the FFT of your marked region peaks at 50.0 / 54.5 / 66.7 px. Your three marks sit right in that zone.

def forward_warp(src, disp_px, z_window=Z_WINDOW, block=512):
    """Forward-warp: each SOURCE pixel scatters to x + disp, foreground wins.

    Replaces the earlier inverse warp. Inverse warp sampled disparity at the
    destination, which at a depth step drags background pixels along with the
    foreground (the edge smear). Forward warp moves each surface by its own
    disparity and lets the nearer surface (larger disp) overwrite the farther one
    via a z-priority scatter; the gap revealed behind a foreground edge
    (disocclusion) is filled from the background neighbour — which is what the
    other eye actually sees there. Result: crisp silhouettes, clean fills.

    The scatter is SUB-PIXEL (device round 7). It used to land on round(x + disp),
    which quantises disparity to whole pixels — and in the deep-space recipe disp is
    a smooth field with no real occlusion edges, dominated by the cos^power pole
    falloff. Half-disparity there sweeps 13.5px -> 0 from equator to pole, so
    rounding carved it into ~13 integer TERRACES at fixed latitudes on every scene,
    independent of content: a 1px content step in each eye plus a discrete jump in
    apparent depth across each boundary. That is the "banding" report — it reads as
    pronounced arcs in the headset and is almost invisible in a 2D screenshot,
    because most of the signal is the depth step, not the tone step. Splatting each
    source pixel bilinearly across its two neighbouring destinations makes disparity
    continuous, so a smooth depth field warps smoothly.

    Hard z-priority is preserved: a first integer pass finds the winning (nearest)
    surface per destination, and the splat rejects any contribution sitting more
    than `z_window` px behind it. Genuine silhouettes — the grounded recipe's are
    tens of px apart at 1.0% baseline — are therefore untouched; only sub-pixel
    disparity differences, which is exactly the terracing regime, get blended.

    Rows warp independently (the shift is purely horizontal), so this runs in row
    blocks: a full-frame bincount at 12288x6144 would need GB-scale float64 buffers.
    """
    H, W = src.shape[:2]
    srcf = src.astype(np.float32).reshape(H, W, 3)
    out = np.zeros((H, W, 3), np.float32)
    filled = np.zeros((H, W), bool)
    xs = np.arange(W, dtype=np.float32)

    for y0 in range(0, H, block):
        y1 = min(H, y0 + block)
        h = y1 - y0
        d = disp_px[y0:y1].astype(np.float32)
        xf = xs[None, :] + d
        rowoff = (np.arange(h, dtype=np.int64) * W)[:, None]
        n = h * W
        dv = d.ravel()

        # Pass 1 — integer z-priority scatter: which surface owns each destination.
        xr = np.mod(np.round(xf), W).astype(np.int64)
        fl = (rowoff + xr).ravel()
        order = np.argsort(dv, kind="stable")          # ascending: near written last
        zwin = np.full(n, -np.inf, np.float32)
        zwin[fl[order]] = dv[order]

        # Pass 2 — bilinear splat of the winning surface only.
        x0 = np.floor(xf)
        fr = (xf - x0).ravel()
        sf = srcf[y0:y1].reshape(-1, 3)
        acc = np.zeros((n, 3), np.float64)
        wsum = np.zeros(n, np.float64)
        for xi, wgt in ((x0, 1.0 - fr), (x0 + 1.0, fr)):
            dst = (rowoff + np.mod(xi, W).astype(np.int64)).ravel()
            w = np.where(zwin[dst] - dv <= z_window, wgt, 0.0)
            for c in range(3):
                acc[:, c] += np.bincount(dst, weights=w * sf[:, c], minlength=n)
            wsum += np.bincount(dst, weights=w, minlength=n)

        ok = wsum > 1e-6
        blk = np.zeros((n, 3), np.float32)
        blk[ok] = (acc[ok] / wsum[ok, None]).astype(np.float32)
        out[y0:y1] = blk.reshape(h, W, 3)
        filled[y0:y1] = ok.reshape(h, W)

# radius the far field converges to roughly the master's mean colour, which is the
# point — FILL_DETAIL puts fine texture back for diffusion to develop, and fine texture
# has no recognisable morphology to ghost.

# sphere ends up as luminous as the hero and "deep black sky" is lost — the milky
# surround on potm2208a/potm2307a. Dimming toward a floor taken from the master's own
# darks keeps it in-palette (a hard cut to pure black would just move the boundary),
# and it is also what stops the mirror-ghosts that survive the blur, since anything
# still lurking out there is multiplied toward the floor.

FLOOR_PCTL = 10                     # percentile of the master taken as the sky floor
FAR_DETAIL_KEEP = 0.30              # fraction of FILL_DETAIL surviving at full falloff,

        # high-frequency energy to develop into stars and filaments. But it does NOT need

What I changed today:

- **`stereo_synth.py`** — sub-pixel disparity splat replacing `round()`. Verified: 26 terrace rows → 0, and a hard 40 px occlusion edge still transitions in 0 px with the disocclusion filled from background, so the grounded recipe's silhouettes are untouched.
- **`sky360.py`** — mirror-tiled fill → edge-clamp extension (no repeats, so no triptych and no doubled dark gutter); far-field seed texture → seeded noise at the master's own detail energy (I was wrong that fine texture can't ghost — measured p2p 80 in the flank, it was doing most of the ghosting); distance falloff to a floor below the master's darkest pixels; object prompt no longer names the hero. Recipe bumped to **r8**.

Three things need your call before the full run:

1. **HEIC quality** — still blocking from last session. Recommend 0.95 (31 MB/scene, flat-run 136 px vs 50 px at q1.0; galaxy sharpness is flat across all settings now).
2. **The stereo fix hits every scene, not just the 36.** spherex_stars, the SPHEREx/unWISE all-skies and the 15 imported panoramas all go through `process_backdrops.py` and need re-packing too. No diffusion, and SR is cached, so it's just stereo+pack — much faster than the deepsky run, but it's a second pass.
3. **`master_sr.py` still uses the condemned recipe.** It runs UltimateSDUpscale with `seam_fix_mode: "Band Pass"` at denoise 1.0 — the exact thing you rejected as the banding source in sky360. That's what put the tile grid and the staircased limb into saturn1, and all 9 `potm_sr/*.png` masters were built with it. Regenerating them means ~1–2 h more on the pod before the deepsky run can use them.

On saturn1 specifically: the ESA original is ~1103×621, about 0.7 MP — a web-sized file, not an archive master. Nothing recovers detail that was never captured; the ×3.38 is the whole story. Realistic options are to drop it, shrink its fov so it isn't stretched so far, or re-SR it with RealESRGAN. Worth your call rather than mine.

        n = h * W
        dv = d.ravel()

        # Pass 1 — integer z-priority scatter: which surface owns each destination.
        xr = np.mod(np.round(xf), W).astype(np.int64)
        fl = (rowoff + xr).ravel()

        xf = xs[None, :] + d
        rowoff = (np.arange(h, dtype=np.int64) * W)[:, None]
        n = h * W
        # Priority is NEARNESS = |disp|, not the signed shift. `disp` is +0.5*d for the
        # left eye and -0.5*d for the right, so a signed key ranks the right eye's
        # nearest surface LAST and the far one wins every contested pixel — occlusion
        # inverted in one eye only. (Pre-existing: the integer scatter sorted the signed
        # value too. It hid because the common test case has the near surface moving
        # AWAY from the join, which disoccludes instead of contesting.) The left eye is
        # unaffected either way, so the approved look does not move.
        prio = np.abs(d).ravel()

        # Pass 1 — integer z-priority scatter: which surface owns each destination.
        xr = np.mod(np.round(xf), W).astype(np.int64)
        fl = (rowoff + xr).ravel()
        order = np.argsort(prio, kind="stable")        # ascending: nearest written last
        zwin = np.full(n, -np.inf, np.float32)
        zwin[fl[order]] = prio[order]

Pilot's progressing — m8_lagoon outpaint done in 119 s, now on seam close.

On HEIC quality — here's what you're actually looking at, because the framing has changed since that recommendation was written.

**What quality controls.** Not sharpness. Measured last session across q0.85→1.0, galaxy high-frequency detail is flat (HF rms 5.79–6.19) — the lowpass bug was what made low quality *look* soft, and that's fixed. The only thing quality buys now is whether the **TPDF dither survives the encode**. The dither is 1-LSB noise deliberately added before the 8-bit quantise to break up contour bands in near-black sky. Noise is exactly what a lossy codec spends its bit budget removing, so at low quality the encoder strips the dither back out and the bands return. That's the whole trade — you're paying file size to keep noise alive.

**What to look at in the headset.** Large, smooth, *dark* areas well away from the hero — the deep field between the footprint and the pole, and the zenith/nadir caps. Not the nebula, not the galaxy. You're looking for concentric contour rings, broad tonal steps in something that should be a continuous gradient. If the sky reads as smooth gradient, quality is high enough; if you see rings, it isn't.

**But don't decide it yet.** Most of what you've been calling banding turned out to be the stereo disparity terracing, not 8-bit tone banding — those arcs you marked on spherex_stars were `round()` in the warp, and they'd have been there at *any* HEIC quality. So the reference you'd be judging against is contaminated. Once you see an r8 scene with the terracing gone, the remaining tone banding may be mild enough that 0.92 is fine, which would roughly halve the library size versus 0.95.

Concretely: when the pilot lands I can pack one scene at 0.92 / 0.95 / 1.00 into three separate backdrops so you can flip between them in-scene and pick. That's ~2 minutes of packing and it makes the decision empirical instead of a number I recommend.

One correction to flag: the pilot currently running started before I made the occlusion-priority fix, so its stereo pass used the sub-pixel splat but the old signed sort. The diffusion and SR stages are cached under r8, so I'll re-pack the three scenes afterward — that's a minute or two, not another render.

The sky reads as smooth gradient, aside from the stereo field issues we were just discussing. I want to get everything re-rendered with all the fixes and adjustments we've got so far so we can level set. If it will preserve token spend, give me a script to run and I can do it manually. Make the script with descriptive output so I can check the window periodically and see what's going on. Status bars would be especially nice.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Full library re-render — every scene, every fix, one command.

Why this exists: the fixes for the device round-6/7 defects (USDU tile banding, the
180deg seam, the hard footprint box, blobby background galaxies, the pole whirlpool,
the m8_lagoon mirror triptych, the m31 twin subject, the milky surround, and the
stereo disparity terracing) all landed in code while the shipped assets stayed on the
OLD renders. Nothing in the headset had any fix in it. This walks the whole library
back through the pipeline so the assets and the code finally agree.

Two phases, because the library is built by two different pipelines:

  Phase 1  deep-sky scenes  (upscale/deepsky_pipeline.py)
           Flat astrophoto masters -> diffusion 360 sky -> RealESRGAN to 12288 ->
           pole soften -> master re-composite -> stereo -> pack. The expensive one:
           two pod round-trips per scene. Sky-recipe caches are keyed by SKY_RECIPE,
           so a scene already rendered at the current recipe re-runs only the cheap
           tail (SR onward), not the diffusion.

  Phase 2  backdrop scenes  (upscale/process_backdrops.py)
           Imported panoramas, Shutterstock deep-space plates, SPHEREx/unWISE
           all-skies. These never touch sky360 — but they DO go through
           stereo_synth, so they need re-packing to pick up the sub-pixel disparity
           fix. That is the one that removes the latitude arcs, and it is the reason
           this phase is in the list at all.

Progress is written both to the terminal (live status line + per-stage detail) and to
a timestamped log file, so leaving it running and checking back later works fine.
State is journalled after every scene: interrupting with Ctrl-C and re-running picks
up where it stopped instead of starting over.

Run:
    python3 scripts/rerender_all.py                  # everything, resumable
    python3 scripts/rerender_all.py --dry-run        # show the plan, do nothing
    python3 scripts/rerender_all.py --phase 1        # deep-sky only
    python3 scripts/rerender_all.py --only spatial_m8_lagoon
    python3 scripts/rerender_all.py --restart        # ignore previous state
    python3 scripts/rerender_all.py --quality 0.92   # HEIC lossy quality
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.dirname(HERE)
UPSCALE = os.path.join(REPO, "upscale")
BACKDROP = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/Backdrop")
SKY_CACHE = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/_raw/_sky_cache")
STATE = os.path.join(SKY_CACHE, ".rerender_state.json")
LOGDIR = os.path.join(REPO, "upscale", "logs")

# Nominal per-scene wall clock, used only for the ETA before real timings exist.
NOMINAL = {1: 6 * 60, 2: 2 * 60}

C = {"dim": "\x1b[2m", "b": "\x1b[1m", "g": "\x1b[32m", "r": "\x1b[31m",
     "y": "\x1b[33m", "c": "\x1b[36m", "0": "\x1b[0m"}
TTY = sys.stdout.isatty()
if not TTY:
    C = {k: "" for k in C}

# Child stdout lines matching these are pipeline noise, not progress.
NOISE = ("tar: Removing leading", "warning: failed to translate")


def hms(sec):
    sec = int(max(0, sec))
    h, m, s = sec // 3600, (sec % 3600) // 60, sec % 60
    return f"{h}h{m:02d}m" if h else (f"{m}m{s:02d}s" if m else f"{s}s")


class Screen:
    """Terminal output with one live status line pinned to the bottom."""

    def __init__(self, logpath):
        self.log = open(logpath, "a", buffering=1)
        self.status = ""

    def _clear(self):
        if TTY and self.status:
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b[2K\r")
            sys.stdout.flush()

    def line(self, text="", to_log=True):
        self._clear()
        print(text)
        if to_log:
            self.log.write(_strip_ansi(text) + "\n")
        self.redraw()

    def set_status(self, text):
        self.status = text
        self.redraw()

    def redraw(self):
        if TTY and self.status:
            w = shutil.get_terminal_size((100, 24)).columns
            s = self.status
            if len(_strip_ansi(s)) > w - 1:
                s = s[: w - 2] + "…"
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b[2K\r" + s)
            sys.stdout.flush()

    def done(self):
        self._clear()
        self.status = ""
        self.log.close()


def _strip_ansi(s):
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == "\x1b":
            j = s.find("m", i)
            i = len(s) if j < 0 else j + 1
        else:
            out.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return "".join(out)


def bar(done, total, width=30):
    filled = 0 if not total else int(round(width * done / total))
    return "█" * filled + "░" * (width - filled)


def load_manifests():
    """Scene lists, imported from the pipelines themselves so this never drifts."""
    sys.path.insert(0, UPSCALE)
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "scripts"))
    import deepsky_pipeline as dp
    import process_backdrops as pb
    from sky360 import SKY_RECIPE
    phase1 = [(n, k) for (n, _rel, k, _p) in dp.MANIFEST]
    phase2 = [(n, c) for (n, _src, c, _e) in pb.MANIFEST]
    return phase1, phase2, SKY_RECIPE


def preflight(scr, need_pod):
    ok = True

    def check(label, good, detail):
        nonlocal ok
        mark = f"{C['g']}✓{C['0']}" if good else f"{C['r']}✗{C['0']}"
        scr.line(f"    {mark} {label:<20} {detail}")
        ok = ok and good

    pod = ""
    if need_pod:
        r = subprocess.run(["kubectl", "get", "pods", "-n", "ai", "-l", "app=comfyui",
                            "--no-headers", "-o", "custom-columns=:metadata.name"],
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        pod = r.stdout.strip().split("\n")[0] if r.returncode == 0 else ""
        check("comfyui pod", bool(pod), pod or "NOT FOUND — the diffusion stages will fail")
    else:
        scr.line(f"    {C['dim']}·{C['0']} comfyui pod        not needed for this selection")

    sw = shutil.which("swift")
    check("swift", bool(sw), sw or "NOT FOUND — pack_spatial.swift cannot run")

    free = shutil.disk_usage(REPO).free / 1e9
    check("free disk", free > 60, f"{free:.0f} GB free")

    check("backdrop dir", os.path.isdir(BACKDROP), BACKDROP)
    return ok


def run_scene(scr, name, phase, quality, overall, totals, t_start):
    """Run one scene as a child process, streaming its stages. Returns (ok, seconds)."""
    script = "deepsky_pipeline.py" if phase == 1 else "process_backdrops.py"
    cmd = [sys.executable, os.path.join(UPSCALE, script), "--only", name, "--force"]
    env = dict(os.environ, FLOAT_HEIC_QUALITY=str(quality), PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1")

    t0 = time.time()
    stage = "starting"

    def status():
        done, total = overall
        pct = 0 if not total else 100 * done / total
        elapsed = time.time() - t_start
        per = totals["mean"](phase)
        eta = (total - done) * per
        return (f"  {C['c']}[{bar(done, total)}]{C['0']} {done}/{total} {pct:3.0f}%  "
                f"elapsed {hms(elapsed)}  eta {hms(eta)}  "
                f"{C['dim']}▸ {name}: {stage}{C['0']}")

    scr.set_status(status())
    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                         text=True, bufsize=1, env=env, cwd=REPO)
    tail = []
    for raw in p.stdout:
        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip() or any(n in line for n in NOISE):
            continue
        tail.append(line)
        tail[:] = tail[-25:]
        scr.log.write(line + "\n")
        # "[HH:MM:SS]   spatial_x: outpaint (119s)" -> "outpaint (119s)"
        msg = line.split("] ", 1)[1] if line.startswith("[") and "] " in line else line
        msg = msg.strip()
        if msg.startswith(name + ":"):
            msg = msg[len(name) + 1:].strip()
        if msg.startswith("==="):
            continue
        stage = msg
        scr.line(f"    {C['dim']}{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}{C['0']}  {msg}", to_log=False)
        scr.set_status(status())
    rc = p.wait()
    secs = time.time() - t0

    heic = os.path.join(BACKDROP, f"{name}.heic")
    if rc == 0 and os.path.exists(heic):
        mb = os.path.getsize(heic) / 1e6
        scr.line(f"  {C['g']}✓{C['0']} {name}  {hms(secs)}  →  {mb:.1f} MB")
        return True, secs, mb
    scr.line(f"  {C['r']}✗ {name} FAILED (exit {rc}){C['0']}")
    for t in tail[-8:]:
        scr.line(f"      {C['dim']}{t}{C['0']}")
    return False, secs, 0.0


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="print the plan and exit")
    ap.add_argument("--phase", choices=["1", "2", "all"], default="all")
    ap.add_argument("--only", help="one scene name (implies its phase)")
    ap.add_argument("--restart", action="store_true", help="ignore previous state")
    ap.add_argument("--quality", type=float, default=0.95,
                    help="HEIC lossy quality passed as FLOAT_HEIC_QUALITY (default 0.95)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    phase1, phase2, recipe = load_manifests()
    plan = []
    if args.phase in ("1", "all"):
        plan += [(1, n, k) for n, k in phase1]
    if args.phase in ("2", "all"):
        plan += [(2, n, k) for n, k in phase2]
    if args.only:
        plan = [r for r in plan if r[1] == args.only]
        if not plan:
            print(f"no scene named {args.only}")
            return 2

    os.makedirs(LOGDIR, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(SKY_CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    logpath = os.path.join(LOGDIR, f"rerender_{time.strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}.log")

    state = {}
    if os.path.exists(STATE) and not args.restart:
        try:
            state = json.load(open(STATE))
        except Exception:
            state = {}
    # A scene counts as done only if it finished at THIS sky recipe and quality.
    def is_done(n):
        s = state.get(n)
        return bool(s and s.get("ok") and s.get("recipe") == recipe
                    and abs(s.get("quality", -1) - args.quality) < 1e-9)

    todo = [r for r in plan if not is_done(r[1])]
    skipped = len(plan) - len(todo)

    scr = Screen(logpath)
    n1 = sum(1 for r in todo if r[0] == 1)
    n2 = sum(1 for r in todo if r[0] == 2)
    est = n1 * NOMINAL[1] + n2 * NOMINAL[2]

    scr.line("")
    scr.line(f"{C['b']}══ Float — full library re-render ══{C['0']}")
    scr.line("")

# library is bimodal with a wide empty middle, so the exact cut is not delicate.
# Measured over the real library these land in two tight clusters with NOTHING between
# 23 and 55, so the cut is not delicate; the band below just refuses to guess if a
# future master ever lands in the gap.
BORDER_ON_BLACK = 25.0
BORDER_RUNS_OFF = 45.0


def border_level(path):
    """Brightest of the master's four edge medians. High = the subject is cut off by the
    frame and diffusion must CONTINUE it outward (field recipe: mirror-tiled structural
    fill, anchored denoise, continuation prompt). Low = the subject hangs on black and
    diffusion should paint starfield around it, not extend it (object recipe: flat
    border-median fill, high denoise, starfield prompt).

    MAX, not mean, over the four edges: a wide crop of a discrete object has two long
    dark edges that outvote the two short ones, so averaging called the Sombrero and
    Centaurus A "runs off the edge" purely because they are letterboxed."""
    import numpy as np
    with Image.open(path) as im:
        im = im.convert("RGB")
        im.thumbnail((512, 512), Image.LANCZOS)
        a = np.asarray(im, np.float32).mean(2)
    k = max(2, min(a.shape) // 24)
    return float(max(np.median(a[:k]), np.median(a[-k:]),
                     np.median(a[:, :k]), np.median(a[:, -k:])))


def classify(title, path=None):
    t = title.lower()
    if any(k in t for k in PLANET_KW):
        return "planet"
    kw = "field" if any(k in t for k in FIELD_KW) else "object"
    if path is None:
        return kw
    b = border_level(path)
    if b < BORDER_ON_BLACK:
        return "object"
    if b > BORDER_RUNS_OFF:
        return "field"
    return kw

There was an earlier log at 18:40:01, so this run was started once and interrupted. That first attempt's outpaint kept computing on the pod after the Ctrl-C and landed at 18:42. The race itself is real and pre-existing, and right now it's dangerous: the pod's output directory still holds `skyout_*` files from the r6/r7 era for **every** scene, so if it fires again it will silently copy an old outpaint and you'd get another headset session on stale renders.
